fatal_errors: The cited evidence does not support a simultaneous strength and ductility increase relative to the stated as-cast baseline: E2 reports about 25.6% ductility as cast but only about 14% after cryo-rolling and annealing, despite the higher strength.
Critical processing variables such as rolling reduction, strain rate, exact annealing temperature, and annealing duration are unspecified, so the intervention is not reproducible.
The proposed controlled-recrystallization and interface-improvement mechanism is not established by the cited excerpts.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the correct general strength–ductility problem and proposes a testable thermomechanical route, but it does not reconstruct the HPHT intervention, its 6 GPa/1473 K conditions, coherent hierarchical interfaces, deformation-transfer mechanism, or approximately 1150 MPa and 36% elongation outcome. More importantly, it is not a well-supported alternative as written: its evidence supports high strength after cryo-rolling and annealing, but not improved ductility versus its chosen as-cast baseline. The experiment can test the property claim, yet an as-cast-only control cannot isolate cryogenic rolling from annealing or distinguish the asserted mechanism; conventional rolling, rolling-only, and annealing-only controls plus explicit mechanistic failure criteria would be needed.
